goal: Reduce latency for one complete offline batch=32 image inference, preserving the source quality checks.
completion: One measured invocation is resnet_inference.infer(model, pixels) (resnet_inference.py:14-16): one complete forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() on the prebuilt GPU-resident FP32 NCHW batch=32 pixel tensor, bounded by torch.cuda.synchronize() before and after (resnet_inference.py:42-47). The run is complete when the forward has finished and the logits tensor for all 32 images exists; the framework's surrounding synchronization marks the boundary. Excluded from the measured invocation: model loading (from_pretrained(...).cuda().eval()), pixel tensor construction from pixels.npy (resnet_inference.py:23-29), reference construction, close/negative quality checks, reference torch.save, the warmup/repeats statistical loop and result.json writing.
state_protocol: prepare(context, request) applies the source numerics from common.configure() (torch.set_num_threads(4), set_num_interop_threads(1), manual_seed(20261020), TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision='highest') using context['device'], loads ResNetForImageClassification from assets_dir with local_files_only=True and dtype=torch.float32 onto that device in eval mode, loads pixels.npy onto the device, and builds the frozen batch as images[torch.arange(batch, device) % len(images)].contiguous() with batch read from request['workload']['batch']. Model, full image tensor and batch stay in state. reset(state) is effectively a no-op (re-asserts eval()): inference is stateless, run() creates its own request-local output under inference_mode, and the source clears nothing inside its timed invocation, so there is no cache or gradient state to restore. The framework synchronizes and resets CUDA peak stats at its timer boundaries; statistics are queried only in metrics().
invariants: Workload stays the offline row: a single complete forward pass over a contiguous FP32 NCHW batch=32 tensor built as images[torch.arange(32) % 3] from pixels.npy (3 real preprocessed ImageNet-normalized images); batch is read from request['workload']['batch'], not hardcoded.
Model is the provided pretrained ResNet-18 loaded from request['assets'] with local_files_only=True in float32, in eval mode, with no architecture, weight, precision or preprocessing changes.

Numerical policies from common.configure() are preserved: TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision='highest', torch.manual_seed(20261020), num_threads(4), num_interop_threads(1).
The forward runs under torch.inference_mode() exactly as the source infer() does; no grad mode, no autocast.

Quality gates are the source's: full 1000-class logits compared with torch.testing.assert_close at atol=rtol=0.0001, exact top-1 label equality (torch.equal on argmax), and rejection of corrupted outputs; observe() returns every logit and all predicted class integers.

latency_ms is the wall time of one complete batch forward between CUDA syncs (resnet_inference.py:48); at fixed batch=32, images_per_second = batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns is its reciprocal, and peak_allocated_bytes is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated over the timed forward.

Setup/timed separation is preserved: model loading, batch construction and reference checks stay outside run(); nothing inside the timed region is precomputed beyond what the source already holds GPU-resident before its timer (model weights and the pixels batch).
Single-process single-GPU execution on context['device']; no NCCL, no process-group creation, no communication.
assumptions: The request freezes the offline batch=32 row only; the source's online batch=1 row and the held-out unseen_batch=7 workload are not part of this run, and the adapter reads batch from request['workload'] so a variant reuses it unchanged.

request['assets'] paths (assets_dir, pixels_npy) are the local pretrained ResNet-18 fixture; no model download is needed or permitted, and pixels.npy itself constitutes the actual task data (3 real preprocessed public images).
The source quality scope is reference fidelity only (protocol 'readiness_baseline_not_optimization'); no downstream accuracy or convergence claim is made.

The row constraint images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 in workloads.json is scoped to the memory goal of the offline row; the user objective latency_ms carries no performance constraint, but images_per_second and peak_allocated_bytes are still reported as project metrics in their native units.

metrics() derives latency_ms from elapsed_ms and images_per_second as batch*1000/elapsed_ms, matching the source formula at fixed batch; peak_allocated_bytes is read from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() in metrics() after the framework's timed window, mirroring the source's per-sample statistic query.

The optional --profile diagnostic trace (common.py profile_once) is measurement infrastructure separate from the clean timing path and is not reproduced in run(); no set_mode split is needed because the timing path already returns full logits identical to the correctness path.

The framework's timer supplies the CUDA synchronization before and after run() and resets peak stats immediately before timing, matching the source's own sync/reset/sample structure; run() therefore performs only the forward itself.

The device from context['device'] replaces the source's hardcoded configure(device=0)/.cuda(); everything runs on that bound device in a single process (request lists one device, distributed_backend null).
Live GPU allocations at the source timer include the full 3-image pixels tensor held by a source-local variable; state['images'] preserves that allocation.
